candidate.answerReason: Two adjacent radii enclose 360°/6 = 60°, forming an equilateral triangle with a hexagon side. Thus the radius is 2.

methods.label: Equilateral central triangle
methods.explanation: The central angle of a regular hexagon is \(60^\circ\). The center and two adjacent vertices form an equilateral triangle, so the radius equals the side length, 2.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 9 regular-polygon geometry and the Grade 8 equilateral-triangle criterion.
